consumer.title: One Experience Without Pretending Every Provider Is the Same
consumer.body: StreamSuites connects to livestream providers through the capabilities each provider actually supports. Labels remain explicit when a connection is available, partial, paused, credential-gated, scaffolded, or planned.

developer.title: Capability Catalogs and Provider-Specific Contracts
developer.body: Runtime/Auth owns provider capability and integration state. Event normalization, public projections, destination metadata, and creator connection surfaces may share shapes, but provider APIs, permissions, quotas, and output support are not assumed to have parity. Clients render authoritative capability flags instead of inferring readiness.

consumer.title: Provider-Aware Chat Foundations
consumer.body: Live chat, notices, clip requests, and engagement events can support StreamSuites modules where an authorized provider path is implemented, while unavailable paths stay visibly unavailable.

developer.title: Runtime-Owned Workers and Normalization
developer.body: Runtime platform workers and provider services own implemented ingestion, normalization, redacted telemetry, quotas, and lifecycle control. Their current maturity varies by provider and credential posture. Public and production clients do not start duplicate workers or claim a provider is connected solely because a UI scaffold exists.

consumer.title: Connections Stay Account-Owned
consumer.body: Creator integrations and destinations belong to the signed-in creator and are shown only through authorized account surfaces.

developer.title: Protected Credentials and Capability-Gated Use
developer.body: Runtime/Auth owns encrypted or provider-managed credentials, OAuth state, connection status, destination ownership, and safe capability metadata. Public pages never expose stream keys or tokens. Studio, StudioApp, and OBS receive only the scoped credentials or leases required for their implemented workflow.

consumer.title: Private Browser Production Rooms
consumer.body: Browser Studio provides private rooms, guest staging, layouts, branding, browser sources, and direct browser media. It remains closed access and OFF AIR.

developer.title: Cloudflare RealtimeKit Media, Runtime-Owned Authority
developer.body: The React/TypeScript/Vite Studio consumes Runtime/Auth-owned sessions, room state, invitations, roles, permissions, participant credentials, destinations, branding, and chat state. Browser media connects directly to Cloudflare RealtimeKit. Runtime/Auth does not proxy media. Browser recording and broadcast output remain unimplemented; self-hosted LiveKit plus Egress is a later direction.

consumer.title: A Native Windows Production Workspace
consumer.body: StudioApp is the Windows-first native StreamSuites studio for local capture, production, audio, recording, replay, and output foundations.

developer.title: WPF Shell and Supervised C++20 Media Engine
developer.body: StudioApp is not a WebView or wrapped site. Its C#/.NET/WPF shell owns UX, settings, API clients, orchestration, and engine supervision. The native C++20 engine owns local capture, Direct3D composition, WASAPI audio, encoding, recording, replay, and direct output. Runtime/Auth authorizes shared state and protected output leases without carrying media.

consumer.title: StreamSuites Inside an Existing OBS Workflow
consumer.body: StreamSuites Studio for OBS is a separate plugin and integration for creators who continue using OBS. It does not replace OBS, Browser Studio, or StudioApp.

developer.title: OBS-Owned Media with Scoped Receiver Sessions
developer.body: Runtime/Auth brokers short-lived capability-scoped receiver authority. Cloudflare RealtimeKit guest tracks reach loopback-only OBS Browser Sources while OBS retains scenes, sources, mixing, composition, encoding, recording, and streaming. The plugin does not duplicate StudioApp's media engine and is not an OBS fork.

consumer.title: Creator Configuration and Integrations
consumer.body: Creator provides signed-in creators with account, integration, destination, and module configuration through implemented StreamSuites workflows.

developer.title: Permission-Checked Runtime/Auth Client
developer.body: Creator consumes Runtime/Auth session, identity, role, tier, permission, integration, destination, and module APIs. It may perform implemented creator-scoped writes through those APIs, but it does not store canonical credentials or shared state independently.

consumer.title: Protected Operational Surfaces
consumer.body: Administrative and Windows operator tools provide privileged visibility and controlled operations for authorized StreamSuites operators.

developer.title: Runtime/Auth-Enforced Administration
developer.body: Dashboard/Admin writes use Runtime/Auth and remain role- and permission-checked. Runtime-owned Windows desktop tools may access local operator state under their documented boundaries. Public presentation does not grant administrative authority or imply that a static page is the backend.

consumer.title: Operational Signals Stay Separate from Production Media
consumer.body: Notifications, status, and operational controls can support the suite without becoming a media path or competing production application.

developer.title: Separate Lifecycles and Least Privilege
developer.body: Control-plane, alert, and notification workers retain separate bounded lifecycles and scoped authority. They do not ingest or transport Studio, StudioApp, or OBS video and audio, and their failure must not silently create duplicate workers or privileged fallback behavior.

consumer.title: No Placeholder Is a Promise
consumer.body: A named provider or capability is not presented as usable until its current authoritative contract says it is available.

developer.title: Fail Closed on Unknown Capability
developer.body: Clients distinguish unavailable, planned, scaffolded, credential-gated, degraded, and ready states. Unknown or missing capability data fails closed. UI placeholders do not invent provider APIs, output support, connection status, or release commitments.

consumer.title: Profiles, Discovery, and Published Artifacts
consumer.body: Public brings together creator profiles, eligible live discovery, clips, polls, wheels, tallies, scores, progression, and other deliberately published audience experiences.

developer.title: Read-Oriented Runtime/Auth Client
developer.body: Public uses existing public APIs, authorized sessions where required, and runtime-export fallbacks. It preserves slugs, hashes, queries, deep links, route aliases, loading and empty states, and public-visibility rules. It does not create canonical account, live-status, profile, or module state.

consumer.title: The System Explained as a Whole
consumer.body: This page explains how the production products, shared authority, engagement tools, and wider product ecosystem fit together.

developer.title: Editorial Overview with Structured Detail
developer.body: The static editorial sections establish the current Studio-first hierarchy and media boundaries. The manifest-driven records beneath them keep consumer and developer explanations together, preserve stable anchors, and provide expandable technical constraints without duplicating renderer logic.

consumer.title: Technical Depth When It Is Useful
consumer.body: General readers can understand the product story first, then reveal implementation details when they want the deeper architecture.

developer.title: Shared Structured Sources, Audience-Specific Rendering
developer.body: Public renders consumer text with collapsed developer details. Other clients may render the same source material differently for their audience, but no presentation should contradict current Runtime/Auth or product-repository authority.

consumer.title: Shipped Reality and Operator Guidance
consumer.body: StreamSuites Docs explains implemented behavior, constraints, setup, and operations as the suite evolves.

developer.title: Documentation Follows Implemented Contracts
developer.body: Docs is a client of shipped reality, not a roadmap authority. Product and Runtime repositories remain authoritative for current implementation and validation. Documentation must not turn planned LiveKit/Egress work, deferred native capabilities, or incomplete plugin features into current claims.

sections.title: Why Consumer and Developer Text Live Together

consumer.title: Clarity Without Hiding the Boundaries
consumer.body: A readable explanation and an optional technical explanation can stay aligned as the products change.

developer.title: One Record, Stable Anchors, Less Drift
developer.body: Each entry keeps consumer and developer text in the same ordered JSON record. Stable section and entry identifiers preserve deep links, while the Public renderer keeps technical details collapsed by default and accessible through explicit controls.
